analysis.investment_thesis: Anlon screens as a high-ROCE (38%) specialty API maker, but the Magic Formula earnings yield is only ~4.5% (EBIT 31 / EV ~682 Cr) — it's a good business at a demanding price. More damning, operating cash flow has been negative for four straight years while reported EBIT surges, so the ROIC is an accounting figure, not a cash figure.
key_strengths: Reported ROCE 38.12% and ROE 25.52% — top-quartile if real
Operating margin expanded from 7% (2022) to 26% (2025); EBIT CAGR ~97%
Low leverage post-IPO: D/E 0.27, equity jumped from 21 → 80 Cr
key_risks: Earnings yield only ~4.5% (EV/EBITDA 10.9) — fails the 'cheap' leg of Magic Formula
OCF negative 0/4 years; FCF -23 Cr in 2025 despite 21 Cr net profit — working capital/receivables bleed
Tiny 616 Cr micro-cap with lumpy revenue (57→113→67→120) suggesting customer concentration
red_flags: Four-year streak of negative operating cash flow while reporting record profits
Net profit 21 Cr vs OCF -23 Cr in 2025 — 44 Cr gap is a classic earnings-quality warning
Financing CF +19 Cr funding operations — business not self-sustaining
analysis.detailed_analysis: On the Magic Formula two-factor test: Return on Capital looks excellent (ROCE 38%, EBIT/EV ~31/682 = 4.5%), but earnings yield is well below my 12% threshold. So it fails one leg outright. More importantly, the high ROCE is suspect — EBIT grew from 4 to 31 Cr over three years while operating cash flow went the opposite direction (−2 to −23 Cr). That's not a return on capital I can trust; it's revenue being booked into receivables/inventory rather than collected.
